reviewer: The implementing engineer (Claude), reading every answer in the report. This is the engineer's reading, not an independent architecture review.
method: Each assessment was read in full: Sol's answer as shown or, when withheld, the draft its checks withheld, and the direct arm's answer. Each was judged against the case's expectation and reason, the design's recorded facts as the packet presents them, and whether a value would mislead an architect who took it.

sol.right-grounded: right, and built from the design's recorded facts
sol.right-flawed: right in substance with a minor fault
sol.partly-wrong: a consequential fault in otherwise sound advice
sol.wrong: wrong advice shown to the architect
sol.withheld-right-draft: withheld although the draft was right
sol.withheld-wrong-draft: withheld, and the draft was wrong or unsupported

direct.plausible: right in the value that matters, with a minor fault
direct.materially-wrong: a value that would mislead an architect who took it

better.sol: Sol's advice serves the architect better
better.direct: the direct answer serves the architect better

findings.brainAdds: On the bank payment reference, where the design records its own objective, drivers and interfaces, Sol's answers are built from those facts, and three direct answers carry values that would mislead an architect who took them: 16 and 3 replicas where about 24 are needed, and a 10-second timeout on a 2-second path.
brainCosts: Four right drafts were withheld: three because the model filled the threat field on a decision, which could be set aside as refinements already are, and one because the guard read a question as a verified claim and the second pass contradicted itself.

On the two teaching designs, the desk's capacity arithmetic carries the Playbook's example objective, and Sol takes it as the project's load in all four capacity assessments (SP-01, SP-06, WF-01, WF-06); two of them reached the architect.

Sol still made faults its checks missed: 'observed' for an illustrative workload (SP-03), a 10-second timeout against a 2-second target with 'ensuring exactly-once' (SP-04), and products the packet never names (BP-11).
findings.metricsCannotSeeIt: The automated metrics, even corrected, score the direct arm as sound in 23 of 28 against Sol's 20, because the expectations test the class of verdict and a keyword, not the values against the design. Value bands per case would let them see what this reading sees, and adding them is an architect's change to the expectations.

limits: One run of one model; answers differ from run to run.
The control arm is one plain prompt; another prompt or model would answer differently.
The expectations are implementation-authored and need an architect's review.
This reading is the engineer's, not independent review.
